core_conclusion: Thermal noise strongly mixes exact deterministic winding identity, while a weaker stationary directed mean current remains statistically distinguishable from zero through the largest sampled reduced temperature T*=0.70.

design_system.scale_policy: Shared scales for direct comparisons; transformed/log scales only when explicitly labeled and scientifically necessary.
design_system.legend_policy: Compact legends or direct labels placed in data-sparse regions.

provenance.notes: All quantitative evidence panels derive from verified executed simulations. Explicit schematic panels are illustrative only and are not used as numerical evidence.

panels.question: How do the stationary mean lattice-current components vary with temperature and trajectory-level uncertainty?
panels.uncertainty_definition: Trajectory-level 95% intervals; low-T N=500 per T*, high-T pooled two-seed N=1000.
processing_notes: 60 burn cycles and 100 measured cycles under the stationary protocol.

panels.question: Does the joint two-component stationary current remain separated from zero at high temperature?
processing_notes: Plots the Hotelling T^2 statistic divided by the declared 95% critical value; threshold=1.

panels.question: How does directional cycle bias compare with survival of the exact deterministic target winding?
panels.uncertainty_definition: High-temperature bootstrap 95% intervals are encoded in the source data and rendered where resolvable at final size.
processing_notes: C19 timestep-robustness evidence remains in Supporting Information rather than adding a redundant main panel.

caption: Figure 7. Stationary thermal hierarchy from trajectory-level inference. (a) Mean lattice-current components after 60 burn cycles and 100 measured cycles with trajectory-level 95% intervals. Open low-temperature markers use N=500 trajectories per T*, whereas filled T*=0.50–0.70 markers use pooled two-seed N=1000 estimates. (b) The high-temperature Hotelling zero-current statistic divided by its declared 95% critical value remains above the threshold of 1 through T*=0.70; this ratio is not interpreted as a thermal critical scale. (c) The negative-v cycle probability approaches one-half while the exact deterministic target-winding probability falls to approximately the percent level in the high-temperature band. Targeted timestep checks are retained as numerical-robustness evidence in the Supporting Information. No extinction temperature or equilibrium transition is inferred.
